Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with the most likely match.
CMV reference shows leaf distortion/shoestring pattern - somewhat different from the test image. Let me check Verticillium_Wilt.
Verticillium Wilt shows wilting/drooping - not matching the flat mottled leaf in test. Let me check Leaf_Mold.
This Leaf Mold reference is very similar to the test image - same isolated leaf on gray surface with yellow-green mottling. Let me check another Leaf Mold reference.
Excellent match - this Leaf Mold reference closely resembles the test image (isolated leaf on gray surface, yellow-green mottled patches). Let me check a few more candidates to be thorough.
Powdery Mildew shows white spots - doesn't match. Now check Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus.
TSWV shows bronzing/necrotic spots - different from test image. Check Early_Blight.

Early Blight shows distinct dark concentric-ring lesions - clearly different. Need to check more classes. Check Septoria, Gray_Mold, Late_Blight, Bacterial_Speck, Bacterial_Canker, plus non-leaf classes.
Microscopic image - not useful. Check another Late Blight leaf image.
Late Blight shows dark water-soaked lesions - different. Check Bacterial_Speck and Bacterial_Canker.
Need to cover more classes with remaining budget. Check Alternaria, Anthracnose, Southern_Blight, Sclerotinia, Rhizopus, and Southern_Bacterial_Wilt in parallel-style sequence.
Another microscopic image. Used 14 views, 2 remaining. Check Anthracnose and Southern_Blight.

All 16 views used. Summary of findings:

- **Leaf_Mold** (views 3 & 4): Both references showed isolated tomato leaves on gray surface with yellow-green mottled patches — extremely close visual match to the test image
- All other leaf classes (CMV, Verticillium_Wilt, Powdery_Mildew, TSWV, Early_Blight, Septoria, Gray_Mold, Late_Blight, Bacterial_Speck, Bacterial_Canker): showed distinctly different symptoms (spots, lesions, wilting, necrosis, powdery coating)
- Non-leaf classes (Alternaria, Anthracnose, Southern_Blight): microscopic or irrelevant plant parts, not matching

The test image shows a single tomato leaf on a gray surface with pale yellow-green irregular chlorotic patches and no distinct margins — perfectly consistent with Leaf_Mold's description ("discrete yellow spots on upper leaf surface with no definite margins") and visually identical to the CDDM_1036 reference.
